sections.h2: Three Falmouth offices that touch a sale
sections.html:
A sale involves three offices in Falmouth. Bills come from the sheriff, values come from the Property Valuation Administrator (PVA), and the deed goes to the county clerk, who also takes over any bill that turns delinquent. The county's website links to the PVA's own page for parcel lookups and exemption forms.

  • Sheriff: 202 Chapel Street, with tax calls taken at 859-654-4511.
  • County Clerk: Room 1 at 233 Main Street, box 112, Falmouth 41040, telephone 859-654-3380. Weekday service runs 8:30 to 4:00. Saturday service falls on the second and last Saturday of a month, 8:30 until noon, except around holidays.
  • Planning and Zoning: answers for Falmouth and the unincorporated county on floodplains, addresses, code enforcement and plan review.

Only the owner is mailed a statement. Lenders are not on the list, so if your taxes are escrowed, check with the servicer about its copy.

Rural and small, Pendleton County counted 14,800 residents in mid-2025, a gain of about 1.1 percent over April 2020. Falmouth is the seat, with Butler about ten miles north on the Licking River.

  • Housing stock totals 6,341 units, and 74.7 percent of homes are owner-occupied.
  • An owner-occupied house has a midpoint value of $159,800, against $793 for gross rent.
  • Owners pay $1,172 a month with a mortgage and $475 without one.
  • Typical household income is $64,669, and the typical trip to work takes 36.4 minutes.

Zero building permits were logged for 2025, so a buyer here is almost always buying an older house. Because the planning office handles floodplain rules, a house near the Licking should have its flood zone confirmed before listing.

Statements go out around the end of September, in plain envelopes with blue lettering reading "Pendleton County Tax Statement." The sheriff asks owners still waiting around October 12 to call. Payment is taken in cash, by check, or on a debit or credit card, though cards add a convenience fee and American Express is refused.

Counter service stops on county and state holidays and the weekends beside them, such as Thanksgiving week, Christmas week, New Year's, Martin Luther King Day and the afternoon of Good Friday. A drop box at the front door is watched on video. If you leave a check, tuck in the stub torn from the top of your bill plus a phone number, and add a stamped return envelope if you want a receipt. Leave cash out of it.

Any dispute begins with a sit-down at the PVA, either with the office or a deputy. If that fails, file at the clerk's office no later than the workday after public inspection of the roll wraps up. Inspection opens the first Monday of May and runs thirteen days. The board decides on documents, so bring insurance policies, what the house cost to build and comparable listings.

Owners aged 65 and up, plus anyone classified as totally disabled, qualify for the homestead exemption, worth $49,100 off assessed value in the 2025 and 2026 years. The PVA hands out the application.

A delinquent bill becomes a lien that survives a sale, and KRS 134.015(5) lets it last up to eleven years. The closing title search turns it up, and the payoff comes out of the seller's proceeds.

Once April 15 is behind you, the clerk takes over the bill. Interest builds at one percent every month, and Revenue tacks on a clerk charge of 10 percent and an attorney charge of 20 percent. Advertised delinquent bills are posted through a link on the clerk's site. If you are behind, get a written payoff from the clerk before you sign a sales contract. Should an outside investor buy the certificate first, you owe that investor, with more fees added.

sections.h2: What the seller pays the County Clerk at closing
sections.html:
The grantor owes the state fifty cents on each $500 of declared value (KRS 142.050), paid to the clerk ahead of recording.

  • A deed is $50.00 to record, with $3.00 more per page beyond five.
  • A mortgage is $80.00, and releasing one is $46.00.
  • A deed needs a sworn consideration statement from both parties, plus an address where the next tax bill can be sent (KRS 382.135).
  • Transfers between spouses and foreclosure deeds are among the exempt ones.

Fees can shift a little, so ring 859-654-3380 for an exact figure ahead of closing. Then check two things: with the sheriff, whether this year's bill is settled, and with the clerk, whether a delinquent certificate is attached to the parcel. The title company needs the actual tax statement to work out the proration.

sections.h2: Who gets the bill if the house sells midyear?
sections.html:
Each year's value and owner are locked in on January 1. The statement therefore goes to whoever held the house that day, so someone who closes in spring or summer still gets that year's bill. The common fix is a proration at closing, where the buyer repays the seller for the months after the sale and the title company uses the real bill. Hand the statement over early, and give the closing agent the sheriff's number in case a payment has not posted yet.

With escrow, the lender is not on the mailing list. Ask the servicer for its copy of the statement and a record of payments, so the proration rests on real figures.

1. Phone the sheriff, 859-654-4511, to confirm this year is paid and nothing older remains.
  2. Ask the clerk, 859-654-3380, if any certificate or lien is on record.
  3. If the house is near the Licking, have Planning and Zoning confirm its flood zone.
  4. Gather the tax statement and deed details for the title company.
  5. Request one written total for clerk fees and transfer tax.

Selling for cash can skip a lender's inspection and appraisal. It does not skip the tax, lien and recording steps, which all have to finish before the deed is filed.

sections.h2: What to have in hand when you list
sections.html:
A sale goes quicker when your papers are in order. Put together the latest tax statement, proof of payment, your deed and any exemption approval.

Make a note of anything that could change the assessed value and keep photos and receipts. If you disagree with the value, the window to act is the spring inspection, so a sale in the fall means paying the bill as it stands and sorting out the difference with the buyer.

faqs.q: When do Pendleton County tax statements go out?
faqs.a: Near the end of September. Anyone without one by about October 12 should call the sheriff at 859-654-4511.

faqs.q: How large is the late charge after January in Pendleton County?
faqs.a: The sheriff posts 21% for February 1 through April 15, while a bill paid in January carries 5%.

faqs.q: Where is a deed recorded in Pendleton County?
faqs.a: In Falmouth, at the County Clerk's office, 233 Main Street, Room 1. It is open weekdays 8:30 to 4:00 and, on the second and last Saturday, 8:30 to noon.

faqs.q: Who bears the Kentucky transfer tax on a Pendleton County sale?
faqs.a: Kentucky puts it on the seller (the grantor): fifty cents per $500 of declared value, collected by the clerk first.

faqs.q: Is a PVA conference required before a Pendleton County appeal?
faqs.a: Yes. You meet with the PVA or a deputy first, and only then file with the clerk, no later than the workday after inspection ends.
